title: REST API design essentials
idea: A REST API exposes use cases as resources with predictable URLs, one error shape, cursor pagination for lists and an Idempotency-Key for retryable writes.

analogy.text: A parcel counter with numbered slips. Hand in the same slip twice and the clerk gives back your first receipt instead of shipping a second parcel.
analogy.breaks: A clerk may recognise you; the server knows only the key.

points: Name resources as plural nouns; nest only for ownership, like a doctor's slots.
Every error returns one shape: a status code plus a stable error code.
A cursor resumes after the last row seen, so new rows never shift pages.
The server stores each Idempotency-Key with its request and response, then replays it.

parts.label: Method
parts.note: Creates a resource. Repeating it is unsafe on its own, so it carries a key.

parts.label: Collection
parts.note: A plural noun. The verb lives in the method, not in the path.

parts.label: Header
parts.note: A client-chosen id for one intent, unique per caller. Every retry of that intent sends the same value.

parts.label: Body
parts.note: camelCase JSON, validated with zod before the service runs.

parts.label: Status
parts.note: 201 the first time. A replay returns the stored body; this demo sends 200, many APIs repeat 201.

parts.label: Response
parts.note: Failures use one shape instead: an error object with a stable code.

code.title: Pagination and idempotency
code.caption: A layered Express app on a real PostgreSQL: a paged list, an idempotent create, and every error in one shape.

walk.text: No cancel in this demo, so a plain UNIQUE suffices. Page 3's partial index is the real rule.
Keyset pagination: an encoded (not secret) cursor holds the last starts_at and id. A bad one gets 400.
Claim the key. If it exists, replay the stored body or reject a changed request.
A new key: check the slot, insert, and store the response in the same transaction.
Routes stay thin: read input, require the key, call the service.
One error middleware gives every failure the same JSON shape.
Two pages, then 201, a 200 replay, 422, 409, 400 and 404.

pitfalls: Avoid OFFSET for deep pages of live data; rows shift and items repeat or vanish.
Store the Idempotency-Key in the same transaction as the write it protects.
Scope each Idempotency-Key to the caller so one client never replays another's response.

quiz.q: What status does the third POST, k-1 with SL-2, print?
quiz.why: Key k-1 already exists with a different request. The JSONB comparison is false, so the service throws KEY_REUSED, which maps to 422.

takeaway: Nouns for resources, one error shape, cursors for lists, keys for retries.

starters: Should a cancel be POST /appointments/{id}/cancel or PATCH with a status?
How long should the server keep idempotency keys?
When is offset pagination still fine?
